replies.body:
I confirmed this locally. If you raise inside a `chat.completions.stream()` block, the span ends with no `error.type`. The SDK's `ChatCompletionStreamManager.__exit__` just calls `close()` and never passes the exception along, so the stream wrapper never sees it. On main the span doesn't end at all until GC, so this was already broken, but it should record the error.

The proper fix is wrapping `chat.completions.stream()` with a manager wrapper like `ResponseStreamManagerWrapper` so `__exit__` can see the exception. I can add that here with sync and async tests, unless maintainers would rather keep this PR small and take it as a follow-up.

Thanks for checking! Let's handle it in this PR. A stream manager wrapper similar to what Responses does sounds like the right direction. Tests for raising inside the block (sync and async) would be great too.

I added it in ab790f53. `chat.completions.stream()` is now wrapped with `ChatStreamManagerWrapper` / `AsyncChatStreamManagerWrapper`, and there are sync and async tests that raise inside the block and check the span ends with the right `error.type`.

One difference from Responses is that I didn't subclass `SyncStreamManagerWrapper`. `ChatCompletionStream` yields its own event types instead of `ChatCompletionChunk`s, so `ChatStreamWrapper` can't wrap the stream the user gets back. Instead, the manager enters by calling the instrumented `create()`, which already builds the `ChatStreamWrapper` and owns the span. The manager wrapper picks that up through a context var on entry, and in `__exit__` it passes the caller's exception to it before the SDK closes the response. Users still get the SDK's own `ChatCompletionStream`.

I'd be happy to restructure it to go through the shared base class if you'd prefer.

threads.body: If an HTTP hook opens another `create(stream=True)` request during manager entry, its wrapper registers first, so `entered[0]` selects the unrelated stream; a caller exception then closes/fails that stream while the outer span ends successfully. Select the enclosing request's wrapper, which registers last on this entry path, and add sync/async public-client regressions with reentrant hooks. Apply the same selection change in the async manager at lines 344–345.

+    """

+        super().__init__(manager)
+        self._self_stream_wrapper: ChatStreamWrapper | None = None

+        token = _entered_chat_streams.set(entered)
+        try:
+            stream = cast(
+                "ChatCompletionStream[ResponseFormatT]",
+                self.__wrapped__.__enter__(),
+            )
+        finally:
+            _entered_chat_streams.reset(token)
+        if entered and isinstance(entered[0], ChatStreamWrapper):
+            self._self_stream_wrapper = entered[0]

replies.body:
Fixed in dc5e2a10. If a hook opens another `create(stream=True)` while the manager is entering, that stream's wrapper gets registered first, so `entered[0]` picked the wrong one and the outer span never recorded the caller's exception. Both managers now use `entered[-1]`. The outer request's wrapper is only created after its response arrives, so it's always registered last.

I also added sync and async tests that open a nested stream from an httpx response hook, raise inside the block, and check the error lands on the outer span. Both fail without the fix.
